name: Kaiserbach Klamm
kurzbeschreibung: The wild Kaiserbach-Schlucht near Kaisers in Außerfern thrills with rushing mountain torrents, a 76 m suspension bridge, and alpine tranquility.
preis: Kostenlos (kein Eintritt für Schlucht und Hängebrücke)
oeffnungszeiten: Schneefrei Mai–Okt/Nov 24/7 frei zugänglich (im Winter schneebedingt gesperrt)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Kaiserbach-Schlucht (also known as Kaiserbachklamm) is a wildly romantic natural gem in the district of Reutte (Außerfern) at the transition between the Tyrolean Lechtal and the Lechtaler Alpen. Carved deep between rugged rock faces, the untamed Kaiserbach winds down from the district's highest-altitude municipality—the tranquil mountain village of Kaisers at 1,518 metres above sea level—to its confluence with the Lech near Steeg. Enclosed by steep limestone cliffs, pristine mixed mountain forests, and thundering cascades, the gorge area offers hikers and nature enthusiasts an authentic alpine experience far removed from mass tourism.

Gorge, Nature & Suspension Bridge

The Kaiserbach originates in the high-alpine Kaisertal at the foot of the Valluga, draining the mighty cirques of the western Lechtaler Alpen. Over millennia, the torrent carved a deep chasm into the dolomitic bedrock. The absolute highlight and architectural landmark of the gorge is the Hängebrücke Kaisers (Hängebrücke Kienberg), ceremonially opened in the summer of 2015: this spectacular suspension bridge spans 76 metres at a dizzying height of around 30 metres above the roaring gorge of the Kaiserbach. Crossing the gently swaying structure reveals breathtaking downwards views into the giant potholes and swirling cascades far below the grated walkway. The suspension bridge forms the centerpiece of the popular Rundwanderwegs Kienberg–Kaisers circular trail and seamlessly connects the valley with the route network of the long-distance trail Lechweg. Natural resting areas and informative display boards along the gorge path invite visitors to linger and observe nature.

Visit & Getting There

The Kaiserbach-Schlucht and the suspension bridge are freely and openly accessible free of charge during the snow-free months (approx. May to late October/November; in winter, access is closed or restricted depending on snow and ice conditions). The circular hike from Steeg/Kienberg across the suspension bridge takes around 1.5 to 2 hours. Arrival by car: via the B198 (Lechtalstraße) to Steeg in the Lechtal, where you turn onto the narrow, winding mountain road L283 towards Kaisers; parking is available in the district of Kienberg or directly in the village centre of Kaisers. By public transport: take ÖBB trains to Bahnhof Reutte in Tirol, then Postbus route 110 through the Lechtal to Steeg, continuing up to Kaisers on the regional Tälerbus.

Tips

The trail through the gorge and across the suspension bridge requires sturdy mountain footwear and surefootedness; the rocky and root-strewn path is not accessible for wheelchairs or standard prams. Those suffering from vertigo should approach the suspension bridge at their own pace. After the hike, a stop at one of the rustic alpine inns in Kaisers (such as Gasthaus Vallugablick) is highly recommended, serving traditional Tyrolean fare alongside glorious panoramic views.
